public_rationale: Company-wide losses do not show that every paying customer loses money or that adding subscribers worsens cash burn. A reported positive paid-user compute margin at the end of 2024 is material counterevidence to that inference. But compute margin excludes other attributable costs and does not measure incremental cash burn. The available evidence therefore neither supports nor decisively contradicts the full assertion on a comparable basis.
limitations: The margin report relies on an unnamed source and secondary coverage.
A narrower claim that every paying customer fails to cover compute costs would face stronger counterevidence.
The rhetorical statement about being a real company is excluded from the financial assessment.

our_interpretation: Read every single paying customer literally: each customer's attributable costs exceed the revenue received from that customer.
Read the subscriber-growth statement as an additional causal assertion that incremental paying subscribers worsen net cash burn, rather than merely increasing gross costs.
Use calendar 2024, the latest full annual reporting period underlying the surrounding financial discussion. The sentence itself supplies no period.
The plain reading concerns customer economics; dividing company-wide losses equally across customers does not establish it.
Treat not a real company as rhetorical judgment, not a separate claim about legal incorporation.
The press-estimate accounting basis follows the financial reporting used in the surrounding argument, but no customer-cost allocation method is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Customer-level or exhaustive cohort evidence establishes losses across every paying customer, and incremental-cost evidence shows that adding paid subscribers worsened net cash burn during the target period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence identifies a paying customer or cohort with positive profit after attributable costs, or establishes that additional paid subscribers improved net cash burn. Evidence must cover more than a narrower cost category.
